newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica slides on connection charge woes.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica slides on connection charge woes.

text.p: Telefonica was sharply lower on Monday, hit by fears that Spain is planning to approve much lower connection charges for second operator Retevision than Telefonica had requested, dealers said.
At 1545 GMT, Telefonica was down 100 pesetas, or 2.89 percent, to 3,365, while the Ibex-35 index of leading stocks was off 1.62 percent to 5,477.21.

The government is expected to approve a connection charge of between two and 2.5 pesetas per minute for Spain's second operator to use Telefonica's lines, versus the seven pesetas per minute requested by the telephone giant itself.

"It seems the government, having forced Retevision to be privatised long before it is really ready, is now going to compensate the firm by approving a cheap connection charge, which would mean substantially less income for Telefonica, and stronger competition," said a trader at a Spanish brokerage.
Retevision is due to be 60 percent privatised in April. By the year-end, it is expected to provide direct competition for Telefonica for the first time in basic telephone services in Spain.
A dealer at a foreign brokerage said sellers of Telefonica were European final investors, in particular U.K. funds.
Much will depend on how successful the second operator is, but Telefonica could see substantial additional income from Retevision's operations, according to an analyst who requested anonymity.
"But this would be quite a lot less if the government approves a connection charge of two pesetas per minute," he added.
